statement: IDC says NAND and DRAM costs continue to rise, up over 300 percent year on year, in what it calls a memory crisis.
why: Memory is the single largest cost and supply constraint sitting next to the accelerator itself, so a cost spike of this scale signals a genuinely tight memory chain rather than a normal price cycle.

impact.mechanism: Sharply higher memory costs raise the bill of materials for accelerator systems and squeeze every other device class competing for the same wafers, tightening effective supply.

evidence.excerpt: NAND and DRAM costs continue to rise, up over 300% YoY.

confidence.basis: Analyst-firm blog, a single secondary source; the cost figure is stated as 'over 300%' without a precise level, so no measured value is claimed.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 2 -> 3; sources: IDC (blog)
